matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the overall numeric difference between the two sides; this guides which value changes are needed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Skipping the conversion and assuming the equation is already balanced, leading to an incorrect solution.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be removed from one character and added to another, ensuring both resulting symbols remain valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When generating candidate moves after computing the discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Considering only moves that change numerals and ignoring moves that involve operators, missing the correct solution.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the numeric values of the affected numerals change and compare the net change to the previously computed discrepancy; keep only moves that close the gap.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After listing candidate moves, to filter them.
matchstick.example: Choosing a move that changes a numeral by +5 when the discrepancy is +3, resulting in a still‑incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a '-' while keeping the operator valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests a sign change on a term.
matchstick.example: Leaving the '+' unchanged even though converting it to '-' would provide the needed -2 contribution.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral changes its value by the needed amount, consider moving a stick from an operator (e.g., '+' or '-') to that numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick removed from an operator creates a valid new operator and the same stick can increase a numeral appropriately.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a numeral to an operator but not the other way around, missing the solution that requires a stick from '+' to a numeral.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', each side must have at least one numeral, and all operators must be valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any proposed stick relocation, before accepting the solution.
matchstick.example: Creating an equation with two '=' signs or with a missing operator, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Use a lookup of common single‑stick numeral changes (e.g., V↔X (+5), I↔V (+4), I↔X (+9)) to quickly assess how a stick move alters a numeral’s value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating the numeric impact of adding or removing a stick from a numeral.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn I into V by moving a single stick, which actually requires more than one stick, leading to an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator sign change impact
matchstick.principle: If a stick move changes an operator (e.g., '+' to '-'), account for the sign reversal in the numeric contribution of the adjacent term.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever an operator is altered by a stick move.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' but still adding the term’s value instead of subtracting it, leaving the equation unbalanced.

matchstick.title: Single‑stick move feasibility
matchstick.principle: When proposing a stick relocation, ensure the source character can lose a stick and the destination character can gain it without violating shape rules (e.g., removing a diagonal from X leaves an invalid symbol).
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation, to discard moves that would produce invalid characters.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Increment numeral by adding a vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical matchstick to an I creates II (value +1) and adding it to a II creates III (value +1); this transformation is valid and often needed when moving a stick from a '+' operator to a numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a vertical stick is available (e.g., from a '+' operator) and a numeral I or II can be increased by one to achieve the required numeric change.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to a V, which does not produce a valid numeral, instead of adding it to an I or II.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver focuses on numeric balance and forgets that each symbol must still correspond to a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, verify that every character matches a known Roman numeral or operator shape.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver assumes the move will fix the equation without recomputing the values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recalculate the integer values of both sides after the move and confirm they are equal before finalizing.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the process of moving sticks, the solver may accidentally delete a symbol or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain a copy of the original equation and ensure the final string contains the same number of symbols (except for the changed ones).

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: When an operator changes (e.g., '+' to '-'), the solver forgets that the term’s contribution flips sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Whenever an operator is altered, recompute the term’s contribution with the new sign.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver may inadvertently add or remove a stick instead of relocating a single one.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the source and destination of exactly one stick; ensure no extra sticks appear or disappear.
